source.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro Deep Think Demo | Competitive coding problem
source.description:
Watch as Tong He, a research scientist at Google DeepMind, introduces the new Gemini 2.5 Pro Deep Think, an enhanced reasoning mode that uses parallel thinking techniques.

See how Deep Think uses its reasoning capabilities to tackle a challenging coding problem from the competitive coding platform ‘Codeforces’.

Learn more at https://blog.google/technology/google-deepmind/google-gemini-updates-io-2025/

---

Add us on Linkedin   / deepmind

actual_summary.boundary: All five core_points retain the full supplied source excerpts, including noise. Compare against all core_points, not merely the truncated one_sentence_summary. The historical Summary Evidence ids are preserved, not substituted for the current five canonical distillation ids. No Summary or oracle text is to be added to model input.

source_quality_limits.fact: The video title identifies a Gemini 2.5 Pro Deep Think demo; automatic caption text repeatedly spells DeepSeek/Deep Seek. Preserve both as captured.
source_quality_limits.evaluation: Allow conservative reference to the enhanced reasoning mode in this Google DeepMind-published Gemini demo. Do not force spelling/person-name repair or infer DeepSeek-company product ownership from this caption token.

source_quality_limits.fact: Description names Tong He; the automatic introduction renders Tom.
source_quality_limits.evaluation: The source describes a research scientist at Google DeepMind; using speaker/presenter avoids an unsupported reconciliation. The app user is neither this presenter nor the publisher.

source_quality_limits.fact: The frozen 104 cues contain repeated text and several 10ms continuation fragments.
source_quality_limits.evaluation: No additional independent observations or repeated experiments are implied; text may be summarized without altering frozen Evidence/cues.

source_quality_limits.fact: This review uses the provided captions/metadata/Summary, not video pixels, sound, hidden code or external problem solutions.
source_quality_limits.evaluation: Do not assert what unseen visuals prove, or that no verification exists anywhere; only the provided textual Evidence lacks independent verification.

source_claims_and_numbers.claim: Publisher-presented enhanced reasoning mode built on Gemini 2.5 Pro is said to explore reasoning passes in parallel.
source_claims_and_numbers.modality: Supplier explanation, not independently measured mechanism or a quantified pass count.

source_claims_and_numbers.claim: The presented Codeforces Catch the Mole example concerns a hidden position moving in a tree, responding to queries; wrong guesses are described as moving it toward the root.
source_claims_and_numbers.modality: Task description as narrated, not a complete formal problem specification or reproduced implementation.

source_claims_and_numbers.claim: 160 is the narrated task query cap.
source_claims_and_numbers.number_boundary: Not an observed exact used-query count, reasoning-pass count, model-call count, success rate, latency/token/cost measurement or general capacity guarantee.

source_claims_and_numbers.claim: The presenter contrasts simpler approaches and claims a solution tracking possible positions and using minimax to narrow uncertainty after queries.
source_claims_and_numbers.modality: Attribute the claimed solution/efficacy; the provided text does not independently establish correctness, optimality or superiority across tasks.

source_claims_and_numbers.claim: The source presents this as one coding-performance example, with trusted-tester Gemini API access then and wider access planned soon.
source_claims_and_numbers.modality: Historical supplier statement at the 2025 publication, not a verified current availability/date/price/general benchmark.

expectation.fit_reason: Original interests include reasoning reliability, human verification and test-time exploration. This specific interactive task links actions to changing hidden state and a finite query budget; it supports an explicit, conditional evaluation judgment beyond repeating the vendor demo. Textual naming noise limits attribution but does not erase these internally coherent task/strategy claims.
expectation.minimum_retention_value: A revisable inference that evaluating inference-time reasoning for such tasks should test feedback-consistent state/uncertainty tracking under the task query constraint, with independently reproducible checks, rather than treating a vendor-selected coding demonstration or unmeasured parallel exploration as broad capability proof.
minimum_substantive_judgment: Tie the retained inference to at least two concrete source features: query-dependent movement of hidden state; possible-position tracking/reported minimax uncertainty reduction; finite task query cap.

Explain an original-interest decision or validation consequence, such as verifying consistency of the evolving candidate-state set and compliance with the task query budget in reproducible solutions, not just reporting the named strategy or praising coding performance.

Separate this evaluation inference/hypothesis from the presenter's attributed solution claim. It must remain conditional on source/solution verification and must not assert generic model superiority or proven correctness.
A materially different source-bounded, revisable judgment of comparable specificity and interest relevance may pass; no fixed answer wording is required.
expectation.appropriate_claim_classification: A central extrapolation/evaluation judgment is SYSTEM_INFERENCE or a clearly bounded hypothesis, not an advertised source-proven fact. Attributed source details remain distinct.
retain: Publisher/presenter attribution; app user not assigned the speaker's experiences or beliefs.
The stateful, query-dependent nature of this particular narrated task, and the distinct role of its query cap.
The reported uncertainty-management/minimax strategy versus independently verified correctness.
What would need checking before broader reliability or research-use conclusions; no quantitative/percentage confidence.
Conservative naming or explicit caption/metadata uncertainty; no forced reconstruction of ambiguous names.
not_enough_for_positive: A cleaner/shorter Summary of the five source excerpts.
A bare claim that minimax or parallel thinking improves reasoning.
A generic warning to test models without tying it to this task's dynamic feedback and query constraint.
Rollout news, named entities, unsupported performance praise or repeated caption lines as extra evidence.
forbid: Reassigning the source narrative or research to the product user.
Claiming independently proven algorithm correctness, optimal minimax, universal coding/reasoning superiority or a benchmark gain from this single supplier narrative.
Presenting 160 as actually consumed queries, reasoning passes, model calls, tokens, latency, price or success statistics.
Inventing numeric parallel-pass counts, complexity bounds, tree size, Codeforces rank/problem id, dates, measured cost or performance.
Treating automatic-caption DeepSeek tokens as independent proof of another company's product or demanding an unresolved person-name correction.
Turning historical trusted-tester/planned access into current or guaranteed general availability.
Inferring facts from unreviewed audio, on-screen code, test executions or visual benchmark outcomes.
expectation.confidence: Bounded qualitative partial/low confidence in the extrapolation; source-claim attribution and validation needs explicit. No invented percentages.
expectation.no_new_boundary: NO_NEW remains a legal successful product outcome when a grounded substantive judgment cannot be supported or source noise prevents safe use. It does not meet this positive diagnostic, must not be rewritten into success, and must never trigger forced admission, oracle/input edits or automatic re-execution.
